title: Separate the Three
hook: Three problems. You cannot fix all three.
scene: Heavy rain at dusk on a downtown block that stacked its problems. Ahead: an open van door, a person in the travel lane, a bike splitting the two. You can slow. You cannot thread all three. Hazard management is picking an order — dump speed, give the person the lane, let the bike declare, then deal with the door. Trying to fix all three in one steer is how you write a fourth.
decision: Door, person, bike, all in the next two lengths. What do you do first?

options.text: Steer through the middle and miss all three at once
options.result: You invent a path that does not exist. The bike goes left, the person goes right, the door stays a door. You collect two of them. One steer is not three answers.

options.text: Honk and take the left so they all have to sort themselves
options.result: The horn makes all three move at once, in three directions. You still have to pick one. You picked noise. The left had a van you did not have.

options.text: Speed up and clear the block before they finish stacking
options.result: You add speed to a pile. The person is not done. The door is still open. Faster is how a stack becomes a crash. You did not separate anything.

options.text: Dump speed first, hold, let the person and the bike declare, then creep past the door
options.result: You plant the number. The person finishes. The bike takes a side. The door is the last thing and you creep it. Three problems, three beats. No fourth.

debrief: You cannot fix three hazards in one move. Dump speed, separate them, take them in order. Three problems, three beats, no fourth.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part one
source.teaching_target: When multiple hazards appear at once, reduce speed and separate them; do not try to solve all three in one steering input.
